india_trends.title: Solar powers non-fossil capacity past 300 GW
india_trends.summary: India’s non-fossil power capacity has crossed 300 GW, reaching 60% of its 500-GW target for 2030. Solar leads with 164.59 GW, while non-fossil sources now account for more than 54% of the country’s total installed generation capacity.

india_trends.title: FSSAI crackdown in consumer interest, says Britannia chief Rakshit Hargave
india_trends.summary: Britannia Industries MD Rakshit Hargave backed FSSAI’s crackdown on packaged foods and beverages, saying consumer interests should be protected. Britannia is also strengthening its regional strategy amid rising competition and plans price increases of 1.5-2% in the second quarter.

india_trends.title: Ironhill India crafts overseas merger with US beer chain
india_trends.summary: Ironhill has acquired its US namesake through bankruptcy proceedings, creating a ₹450-crore hospitality group. The Indian microbrewery chain has invested about $7 million in the US business and plans to expand its combined network to around 43 outlets by 2030.

india_trends.title: Acme Solar plans to spend up to Rs 20k crore on capex: CEO
india_trends.summary: ACME Solar Holdings plans to invest ₹15,000-20,000 crore to expand its renewable energy business, with battery storage as a key focus. The company aims to deploy about 10 GWh of battery capacity this year and enter the data centre power market.

india_trends.title: Global banks are pulling back credit cards once prized by rich Indians
india_trends.summary: Several offshore banks are becoming reluctant to issue or renew international credit cards for wealthy resident Indians due to India’s 180-day rule on deploying overseas funds. The requirement is also creating difficulties for minors holding foreign accounts under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme.

india_trends.title: REITs set to gain tax flexibility, cash flow boost under new Bill
india_trends.summary: Indian REITs could gain greater tax flexibility under the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which allows SPVs to opt for concessional corporate tax rates, avoid future MAT and use accumulated MAT credits while retaining tax-exempt dividends for unitholders.

india_trends.title: India can diversify exports away from US if 100% tariffs imposed, has $200 bn market in 15 other countries: Economist SP Sharma
india_trends.summary: India could diversify exports if the US imposes steep tariffs linked to Russian crude purchases, economist SP Sharma said. He estimates a $200-billion opportunity across 15 alternative markets for products India currently exports to the US, including Europe and West Asia.
